title: Digital building permitting still broken — 22% of municipalities report blocked projects
money_note: ~200M CZK (~8M EUR) documented state spend on the non-functional DSR system; billions in sector losses claimed
summary: CKAIT (chamber of authorized engineers) documents ongoing failures of the digital building-permitting system (DSR): per a municipal survey 43% of respondents see delays and complications and 22% of city/municipality representatives say key projects are fundamentally delayed and territorial development blocked; the non-functional system has already cost the state ~200M CZK. CKAIT chair Spalek calls the pending building-act amendment 'worse than the botched digitalization' (Jan 2026).
notes: Z+i CKAIT issue 2026-03 (month-end date used); denik.cz reports DSR 2.0 planned. Portal stavebnika functional only partially since Jul 2024. Demand: permit-preparation tooling, EED document validation, municipal workarounds — and a case study in failed govtech procurement.

title: GP shortage — 483,000 people without a registered practitioner, aging workforce
money_note: State subsidises GP/pediatric practices with up to 900M CZK/yr (~36M EUR recurring); 2025: 140 GP + 70 pediatric + 30 psychiatrist positions supported
summary: Health-ministry data (2025-07-03) document ~5% of the population without a registered GP — 449,000 adults and 34,000 children — while the GP association puts it up to 1 million; ~5,000 adult GPs and ~2,000 pediatricians serve the country and pediatric practices keep declining. Professional-chamber data add the structural cliff: average GP age 57, over 40% of GPs above 60, more than a quarter of specialists over 65, with a 25-30% capacity loss projected within a decade.
notes: Worst: Assko, Karlovy Vary periphery, parts of Central Bohemia; Stredocesky and Ustecky kraj worst for ambulatory specialists. Aging figures: zdravotnickeodbory.cz (Feb 2024), Forbes.cz, tribune.cz; CLK warns quality of care already threatened (lkcr.cz). Demand: practice-succession marketplaces, capacity analytics, telemedicine for uncovered regions.

title: HK CR survey — labor market and bureaucracy top 2026 business obstacles
summary: The Czech Chamber of Commerce's survey of 450 firms documents the biggest expected 2026 obstacles: 58% high labor costs, 51% shortage of qualified workers, ~48% growing administrative burden; in construction 70.9% of firms name worker shortage as the priority problem. The chamber states these obstacles have persisted for years and demand structural policy change.
notes: Press release January 2026 (day not stated on syndicated copies; record dated at scan run). Recurring survey — harvest each January. Pairs with ombud-vek-diskriminace: firms report shortage while measurably rejecting 40+ applicants.

title: Brno participatory budget — ~1,200 citizen proposals in 9 years, 65 delivered
money_note: 35M CZK (~1.4M EUR) allocated annually for realization; max 10M CZK per district
summary: Brno's Dame na vas participatory budget documents citizen demand at scale: ~1,200 project proposals submitted and 142,000+ voters over nine years, yet only 65 projects completed with 26 in progress — a delivery backlog that itself documents municipal execution capacity as the bottleneck. The 2026 cycle allocates 35M CZK, with voting Nov 1-30, 2026.
notes: Aggregates from archspace.cz and kultino.cz coverage of the portal, 2026; portal lists every proposal with status — scrapeable inventory of repeated citizen asks (typically greenery, playgrounds, public space, mobility). Praha has no central equivalent (per-district PBs + Zmente.to app).

title: E-shop compliance collapse — 85% of 751 inspected shops broke the law in 2025
summary: COI's 2025 distance-selling results (published 2026-02-26) document 751 e-shop inspections with violations in 639 (85%), 2,399 individual breaches, and 12,978,500 CZK in fines across 646 closed cases. Top failures: missing complaint-handling information (363), unfair commercial practices (318), missing pre-contractual information (488) and non-compliant order buttons (107).
notes: COI continues e-shops as a 2026 priority (Q2/2026: 103 risk-targeted inspections, 91% violation rate; Q1/2026: 652 discount-labelling inspections, ~40% violations). Accessibility-act enforcement adds to the same audience. Demand: e-shop compliance audit/SaaS; 2,399 breaches = checklistable items.

title: CSDDD implementation guidelines — EU consultation closing 14 Aug 2026
summary: The European Commission's Have Your Say consultation on CSDDD due-diligence implementation guidelines runs 12 June - 14 August 2026, with SMEs documenting adjustment burdens and 360+ CSOs contesting the Omnibus rollback — evidence that supply-chain due-diligence obligations remain unsettled and companies lack practical guidance. Czech exporters in EU value chains will implement whatever the guidelines fix.
notes: Deadline 2026-08-14 (extended). Register already tracks CSRD/CSDDD omnibus (reg-csrd-post-omnibus); this consultation documents the demand side: firms asking for templates, guidance, tooling. Have Your Say feedback is public and countable per initiative.

title: Digital Fairness Act consultation — documented dark-pattern and cancellation harm
summary: The Commission's DFA consultation (17 Jul - 24 Oct 2025; summary report 19 Dec 2025) collected unusually broad documented complaints about manipulative interface design including toward minors, addictive design, opaque personalization, misleading influencer marketing, and friction in online subscription cancellations. The legislative proposal is expected in 2026 and will hit every consumer-facing platform and e-shop.
notes: Summary report 2025-12-19; official page: ec.europa.eu Have Your Say initiative 14622 (Digital Fairness Act). Notable: mass mobilization of gaming communities (game preservation). CZ angle: MPO report names DFA a priority; COI already fines dark-pattern-adjacent practices (318 unfair-practice breaches 2025).

title: Digital Omnibus call for evidence — 25-35% admin-burden cut on data/cyber/AI rules
summary: The Commission's call for evidence on the Digital Omnibus documents the simplification demand around EU digital law (data, cybersecurity, AI): the stated target is cutting administrative burden at least 25% for all companies and 35% for SMEs. The submissions themselves are documented statements of what compliance obligations firms find unworkable.
notes: Reported via AI Act Newsletter #87 and Commission channels; record dated at scan run (exact window on Have Your Say). For the pipeline: the Have Your Say API exposes initiative feedback counts and attachments — harvestable evidence of pain per regulation.

title: Energy billing complaints — missing invoices and unreturned overpayments lead 2025
summary: ERU documents that 2025 consumer complaints were dominated by missing billing statements and unreturned overpayments from suppliers, with 622 consumers escalating to formal dispute proposals against suppliers or intermediaries; roughly every third submission is misdirected (unregulated price components, complaints belonging to suppliers), showing consumers cannot navigate the market's responsibility split.
notes: ERU newsroom summary of 2025 ('O cem jsme psali v roce 2025'; page undated — scan-run date used). ADR series: ERU ~2,200 filings 2020-H1/2025, rising, electricity first (MPO report Table 1). Demand: billing-verification and switching-hygiene tools; supplier-side billing QA.

title: Financial arbiter caseload explosion — consumer-credit disputes up 4.5x in two years
summary: The financial arbiter's 2025 annual report (published 2026-05-29) documents 12,050 new proceedings in 2025 (vs 5,683 in 2024 and 2,660 in 2023, +113% YoY), with consumer-credit disputes at 14,235 of 15,446 running proceedings (~92%), driven from 2,097 (2023) to 11,386 (2025). By the report date 2026 had already brought 8,200 new filings, projecting ~20,000 for the year.
notes: Avg proceeding 167 days; 83% of concluded cases end in settlement. Disputes dominated by creditworthiness-assessment claims (uveruschopnost) — mass-scale claims industry emerging. Demand: dispute-handling automation for lenders, claim triage, settlement tooling. ADR totals 2020-H1/2025: FA ~18,700 filings (MPO report).

title: ADR filings map recurring consumer harm — 45k+ filings 2020-H1/2025 across sectors
summary: The MPO report tabulates out-of-court dispute filings 2020-H1/2025: FA ~18,700 (consumer credit, strongly rising), COI ~18,000 (defective goods and warranties, stable), CTU ~4,200 (dominated by postal services, strongly rising), ERU ~2,200 (electricity, rising), KO CAP ~1,250 (insurance payouts), OnlineADR ~380 (air travel). The European Consumer Centre added 3,463 contacts and 1,396 handled cross-border disputes in 2025 (52% success), mostly flights and online purchases.
notes: Table 1, p.29; ESC series p.30. Postal-service complaints dominating CTU ADR is an under-reported niche; energy disputes rising since 2022 intermediary rules. Each column is a recurring-harm vertical for claim-automation products.

title: Market-surveillance bodies underfunded — COI inspections down 29k to 20k on flat budget
money_note: COI approved budget ~408M CZK 2023 (~16.3M EUR/yr recurring), nominally flat vs 411M CZK 2018 — documented as insufficient
summary: MPO's official Strategy progress report (submitted to government March 2026) documents that COI inspections fell from ~29,000 (2018) to ~20,000 (2023) on a nominally flat budget eroded by inflation, staff down 9%, while complaint volume and new duties grew — and cites the European Commission naming underfunding the main barrier to effective enforcement, with CZ below EU average in inspectors per 1M inhabitants. SZPI and SVS report the same financial and personnel undersizing, SVS losing veterinary specialists.
notes: Report p.24-25 with footnoted COI annual-report sources. Consequence documented: 'fewer inspections, slower reaction to risks, limited capacity to protect consumers and ensure fair conditions for businesses.' Regtech/inspection-automation demand signal.

title: Collective redress barely used — one class action since July 2024
summary: MPO documents that since the collective-proceedings act (179/2024 Sb.) took effect in July 2024 exactly one class action has been filed: OnlineADR.cz v. Postylkov s.r.o., where 56 consumers joined, 52 won, and ~1.6M CZK was awarded in 2025. Individual court enforcement stays rare because claims under 10,000 CZK cannot be appealed and cost risk deters consumers — a documented gap between mass harm (45k+ ADR filings) and functioning collective redress.
notes: Report section 4.3.2.5. Qualified entities must be MPO-registered nonprofits (12+ months active); reward up to 16% of recovered amount — an incentive structure waiting for operators. Legaltech: claim aggregation, opt-in management, funding.

title: Debt enforcement — 596,000 people in exekuce, 545bn CZK enforced, 3M proceedings
money_note: 545bn CZK (~21.8bn EUR) is the enforced-debt stock, not an attached budget — money score stays 0
summary: The Mapa zadluzeni (Institute for Prevention and Resolution of Over-indebtedness + PAQ Research) documents 596,000 people in debt enforcement at end-2025 (3 million proceedings, 545bn CZK total), down 20,000 people YoY but with a rising share of multi-execution debtors, plus ~90,000 people in insolvency-discharge. Regional concentration persists: in Bilina 18.6% of the 15+ population is under execution.
notes: Data reference date 2025-12-31; map published 2026 at mapazadluzeni.cz (municipal granularity, downloadable). Peak was 860k people / 4.7M proceedings (2017). Demand: debt-consolidation, employer payroll-deduction tooling, oddluzeni process automation for the ~90k pipeline.

title: Senior loneliness — 13,000+ crisis-line calls a year, loneliness in every fourth
summary: Zivot 90 documents that its 24/7 Senior telefon crisis line handles over 13,000 callers a year with loneliness present in roughly every fourth call; more than 30% of Czechs over 65 live in single-person households and about one in five seniors reports feeling lonely. Demand for the service repeatedly outgrows capacity, as during pandemic surges.
notes: Figures published on zivot90.cz (undated page — scan-run date used) and neztratitsevestari.cz. Pairs with ombud-nelegalni-domovy and the 70%+ fear-of-dependency survey topic. Demand: companionship/telecare services, family-caregiver coordination.

title: State digital services — 102bn CZK ICT spend, only 18% of services fully online
money_note: ~102bn CZK (~4.08bn EUR) state ICT spend over five years per NKU; report published Jan 2026, day not stated, month-end used
summary: NKU documents that state bodies spent ~102bn CZK on ICT in five years, yet only 1,621 of 8,916 services identified for digitalization (18%) are accessible via self-service digital channels. ICT public contracts 2020-2023 alone were 89.15bn CZK, with ~26bn CZK of EU funds (ERDF+RRF) flowing into eGovernment.
notes: 1,621/8,916 services self-service; digitalization 'often just transfers complex processes online without simplification' (NKU annual report 2025 framing, echo24.cz coverage 'Stat je zasukovany a nevykonny'). Right-to-digital-services act obligations already in force.

title: Czech e-health six years late — NKU calls digitalization of healthcare a fiasco
money_note: 158M CZK (~6.3M EUR) spent on e-health strategic goals 2020-2024 per NKU; day of Jan-2026 report not stated, month-end used
summary: NKU's II. summary report on public-administration digitalization (Jan 2026) documents that health-data sharing and the eZadanka e-referral, legally planned for 2020, will arrive in 2026 at the earliest, and core health registries required by law did not exist as of early 2023. 158M CZK was spent on e-health strategic goals 2020-2024 with infrastructure still missing.
notes: Quote: 'Progress in sharing health documentation ... will arrive in 2026 instead of the originally planned 2020.' Six-year slip on two flagship components; every provider and payer touched. NKU report: II. souhrnna zprava o digitalizaci verejne spravy CR (nku.cz id15299, published Jan 2026).

title: Soft-target protection — no functioning national system after eight years
money_note: MSMT school-security funding: 130M CZK program + 200M CZK increase after Dec-2023 attack (~13.2M EUR total attached)
summary: NKU (audit 2021-2025, published 2026-02-09) documents that the Interior Ministry failed to build a functioning national soft-target protection system in eight years: only 2 of 4 pillars exist, no investment program for security equipment, no methodology to identify most-threatened targets, and the advisory board dormant for 3 years 4 months. Activity rose only after the December 2023 Charles University shooting, when MSMT added 200M CZK for school security.
notes: Audited: MV, MK, MSMT, MZ. Education/training halted 2022-2023. Demand side: schools, hospitals and cultural venues are now expected to buy risk assessments, security tech and training with the new money — vendors face a documented, funded need.

title: Overloaded trucks — weighing system detects ~500k violations, ~1% get fined
money_note: >73bn CZK (~2.92bn EUR) state spend on motorway/I-road repairs and maintenance 2019-2023 (recurring spend; not all attributable to overloading)
summary: NKU audit (2019-2024) documents that the high-speed vehicle-weighing system failed its basic function: all 7 scales deployed since 2020 were non-functional over 60% of the time, and of nearly 500,000 detected overloading cases only ~289,000 were forwarded to municipalities with roughly 1% or less ending in a fine (21M CZK collected in four years). Meanwhile the state spent over 73bn CZK on road repairs 2019-2023.
notes: NKU press release 2025-06-09 (audit 23/26). Quote (Jan Kinst): 'The system was simply not set up to function effectively.' Enforcement pipeline broken between RSD detection and municipal offense proceedings — data-handoff/automation gap.

title: University development funding — 30bn CZK distributed with no outcome tracking
money_note: >30bn CZK (~1.2bn EUR) distributed by MSMT to 26 public universities across 600 projects (2017-2023 audit scope)
summary: NKU documents that MSMT distributed over 30bn CZK for higher-education development without measurable objectives, baselines or impact indicators, so nobody can tell what the money improved. In 9 of 13 audited projects universities violated subsidy conditions (late reports, missed target parameters, incomplete or misleading reporting).
notes: Press release 2025-06-16 ('Strategie bez cile'). MSMT published a dissenting stanovisko (msmt.cz). Pattern: strategic documents contain 'only general formulations without deadlines, baseline values, or impact indicators' — recurring across NKU subsidy audits.

title: Unregistered senior-care homes — ombudsman warns of live illegal operations
summary: The deputy ombudsman documents unregistered facilities providing care for seniors operating in Mutenice, Svitavy and Ceske Budejovice, endangering residents' dignity and safety, and warns families not to place relatives there. Recurring inspections show a structural shortage of legal, registered long-term-care capacity that pushes families to illegal providers.
notes: Published 2026-06-23. Live enforcement topic (registration duty, MPSV fines). Demand driver: registered-bed shortage + >30% of 65+ living alone (Zivot 90). Product angle: capacity search/brokerage, compliance tooling for providers.

title: Workplace sexual harassment — only 2 court cases in a decade, systemic underreporting
summary: The ombudsman's office mapped the Czech legal system and found only two workplace sexual-harassment cases reached court in 2015-2024, calling them the tip of the iceberg and documenting that victims lack accessible reporting and redress channels. Employers face rising duties (whistleblowing act, EU directives) with no functioning internal-reporting practice.
notes: Published 2026-07-14. Fits compliance wave already tracked in register (pay transparency, whistleblowing). Demand: internal reporting/investigation tooling and training for employers.

title: Ombudsman Q1 2026 — 2,341 complaints; social security, health and building law lead
summary: The public defender of rights received 2,341 complaints in Q1 2026 (79.3% within mandate), led as always by social security (477), health administration (190) and building/regional development (156); 123 alleged unequal treatment. Full-year 2025 volume was ~7,450 complaints, up from ~7,000 in 2024.
notes: Primary PDF (KVOP-22990/2026/S) read directly: podnety 2341, soc. zabezpeceni 477, zdravotnictvi 190, stavby 156, diskriminace 95. 2025 total 7,450 from Q4-2025 report (KVOP-3214/2026/S). Quarterly cadence — a standing agenda-level complaint index for the register.

title: Ombudsman systemic-problem inventory — ~200 topics, 800 public submissions
summary: The ombudsman's office compiled ~200 systemic problems in the functioning of Czech authorities from its own casework, received 800 submissions from the public, NGOs, social services and municipalities in a dedicated call, and holds 340 improvement recommendations for CZ from international bodies. A 3-year strategic plan selecting priorities follows.
notes: Press release 2026-03-24, referenced in Q1-2026 report section A.3.1. This is literally a curated national problem list — highest-value single document for the register's demand layer; worth requesting/parsing the full inventory.

title: Age discrimination in hiring documented from age 40 — correspondence experiment
summary: A research report by the deputy ombudsman and Masaryk University scientists (published 2026-08-13) documents via a correspondence experiment on the Labour Office job database that chances of getting hired decline already after age 40, with under one-third of men aged 40-55 receiving positive employer responses. Documented, measured hiring discrimination in the middle of a labor market that simultaneously reports acute workforce shortage.
notes: Method: correspondence experiment (fictitious applications), men 40-55. Pairs with HK CR survey (51% of firms cite qualified-worker shortage) — firms reject documented available labor. HR-audit / compliant-hiring tooling angle.

title: Municipalities — unfunded mandates: housing contact points, delegated powers gap
summary: The Association of Towns and Municipalities (SMO CR) documents to the new government that municipalities must run new state-assigned agendas without money — most concretely the housing-support contact points under the new housing law — on top of a structural gap in financing delegated state powers and the shifted burden of non-pedagogical school staff (postponed to January 2026). SMO names these the key risks to municipal service quality in 2026.
notes: Position published Nov 2025 (ceskenoviny.cz 2732238; record dated at scan run). Housing-support law contact points roll out from 2026 — municipalities will need case-management tooling; SMO press stream is a standing unfunded-mandate tracker.

title: Drug shortages — live SUKL unavailability regime with mandatory reporting
summary: SUKL runs a live drug-availability regime: marketing-authorisation holders must report supply starts, interruptions and terminations, and the office flags products with 'omezena dostupnost' when patient needs cannot be covered by substitutes. In 2026 SUKL announced temporary outages of antidepressants, heart-failure, allergy and hypertension medicines, some lasting months.
notes: Amendment to the medicines act (novela zakona o lecivech) added the availability flag and reporting duties; public database + open data (opendata.sukl.cz) make this machine-readable. Third parties already build on it (GLP-1 availability trackers). Pharmacy/prescriber-facing substitution tooling demand.
